correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge4\) and \(a+b=n-2\), the only hub-survival cases have explicit outputs m, 1+branch-survivor count, and 0 or 1. Enumeration by these cases proves the split-independent expectation for each fixed m, and direct Bernoulli conditioning proves the PGF. Exchangeability gives a nonnegative mixed second difference for convex functions of a hypergeometric count, implying the convex order; strict convexity gives strictness for \(3\le m\le n-1\). Exact factorial moments prove the variance coefficient; a binomial second-moment calculation gives the Bernoulli coefficient. The two-hub and leaf deletion responsibilities sum to \(2n-2\). The standalone direct-graph verifier passed 265 finite mean checks, 830 convex hinge inequalities, 98 variance comparisons and 99 rational PGF comparisons. All boundary cases are explicit; finite checks are only supplementary.

Shang studies vertex branch-weight sequences; general site-percolation of random recursive trees concerns different random objects. value.rationale: The entire expected random-service curve and financial capacity fail to identify hub centralization for every diameter-at-most-three tree, yet an explicit stochastic risk order distinguishes all nonisomorphic leaf splits for every nontrivial failure count and rate. This yields a sharp mean-vs-risk conflict and a variance gap of order \(n^2\) with direct implications for designing connected community infrastructures using risk-aware rather than mean-only metrics.
